payload.native_system_prompt:
You are part of an optimization system that improves a given text (i.e. the variable). You are the gradient (feedback) engine. Your only responsibility is to give intelligent and creative feedback and constructive criticism to variables, given an objective specified in <OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION> </OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION> tags. The variables may be solutions to problems, prompts to language models, code, or any other text-based variable. Pay attention to the role description of the variable, and the context in which it is used. You should assume that the variable will be used in a similar context in the future. Only provide strategies, explanations, and methods to change in the variable. DO NOT propose a new version of the variable, that will be the job of the optimizer. Your only job is to send feedback and criticism (compute 'gradients'). For instance, feedback can be in the form of 'Since language models have the X failure mode...', 'Adding X can fix this error because...', 'Removing X can improve the objective function because...', 'Changing X to Y would fix the mistake ...', that gets at the downstream objective.
If a variable is already working well (e.g. the objective function is perfect, an evaluation shows the response is accurate), you should not give feedback.

### Glossary of tags that will be sent to you:
# - <LM_SYSTEM_PROMPT>: The system prompt for the language model.
# - <LM_INPUT>: The input to the language model.
# - <LM_OUTPUT>: The output of the language model.
# - <OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION>: The objective of the optimization task.
# - <VARIABLE>: Specifies the span of the variable.
# - <ROLE>: The role description of the variable.
payload.instruction: transform the black DVD into a white DVD
payload.rubric: Judge requested image editing: yes means all requested changes are complete, no means no requested change has progressed, partial means some progress without complete fulfillment. Unrelated edits are not requested progress. Insufficient evidence stays unresolved.

node.question: Is the DVD visibly white rather than black in the edited image?
node.criteria: Pass if the DVD is visibly white rather than black; fail if it remains black or is visibly another color; unknown if its color cannot be determined.
node.binding: The DVD identified in the original image; it must remain identifiable as a DVD.

node_traces.evidence: The DVD is visibly white in the edited image.
The DVD is visibly white in the edited image and remains identifiable as a disc.

fulfillment: The node is over-crediting the edit: the edited image shows two white disc-like objects, while the source has one small rectangular DVD case/card near the center and a separate black object at right. The traces repeatedly assert that the DVD is white and preserved, but do not establish which edited object corresponds to the source DVD; the apparent white disc at center-left may be a newly introduced object, and the right-hand white disc appears on the dark object. Tighten the binding to track the specific source DVD across images and require direct evidence of its color change and retained DVD identity, rather than treating any white disc plus disc-like shape as fulfillment. Preserve the rubric’s partial/unresolved distinctions when correspondence or identity is uncertain; do not infer “no” solely from the reference label. The repeated high-confidence identical passes indicate a systematic grounding/binding or criterion-application problem, not a transport or schema failure.
s2: Repair the binding so it follows the specific source DVD across the before/after images, using its location and surrounding scene context—not merely any disc-like object in the edited image. The source shows a small rectangular item near the center and a separate dark object at right; the edit shows two white disc-like objects, so correspondence is ambiguous. Keep this identity check distinct from the requested black-to-white change: assess whether the matched source object remains recognizably a DVD, and do not treat whiteness or a central hole alone as proof of either correspondence or completion. Require evidence tied to the matched object; if correspondence or identity is indeterminate, preserve the rubric’s unresolved/partial distinctions rather than confidently passing. The repeated high-confidence passes point to a systematic grounding or criterion-application issue, not a transport/schema failure. Do not force the reference label to determine the node’s result.
